**Get Started Here\!**   
**How to Learn NextJS Quickly** 

* One of the primary goals of Next to expand the use of React to static sites. 

**File-Based Routing** 

* Files and folders (i.e. in src/app) determine what routes exist in your app.   
  * ![app To exit full screen, press esc src v app The 'src/app' folder is a super special folder The files and folders you place in here determine what routes exist in your app C + ûdemy mockups needs app place routes es deep route nested ex ex2][image1]  
* The name of the folder a .tsx file resides in controls the route. 

**Linking Between Pages** 

* Next's built in *Link* component 

**Common UI in Next JS with Layouts** 

* Common layouts like a header can be added to a *layout.tsx* file that would be wrapped around other page components, to reuse content that is needed on all pages. 

**Absolute Path Import Shortcut** 

* @ 

**Adding Images in Next JS** 

* Built in Image component   
* On the server side, It makes several resized versions of your image for different device sizes.   
* The resized version will be cached on the server. 

**More on the Image Component** 

* The built in Next Image component helps avoid content shifting (content loads before the image, causing layout to shift after the image loads) 

**Production Deployment with Vercel** 

* npx vercel   
* Log in with Vercel   
* Prompted to set up and deploy with Vercel   
* Deploy scope   
  * Relevant only if your account is tied to a larger account, like a company   
* Link to existing project   
* Project name   
* Directory of code   
  * Default is ./ which is the root of project folder

**Streaming Content with React Server Components**   
**Introducing Server Actions in Next.js** 

* A server action is a function that will be called with the values a user entered into a form.   
  * It's the number one way to change data in a next app.   
  * Has super close integration with HTML forms   
* use server at the top of a function is a non-standard JavaScript directive used by Next.js. It indicates that the function is a server action. 

**A Deeper Dive into Server Actions** 

* Using Next allows code to be executed from the browser and server in the same code. 

**Server Components vs Client Components** 

* Client component \- A function that returns JSX that rendered into HTML. Uses all features of a React component.   
  * Add use client to the top of the file to indicate it's a client component.   
  * Cannot directly show a Server component   
    * Only exception is (TODO)   
* Server component \- A function that returns JSX, but has some limitations and different capabilities.   
  * More closely integrated with Next.js   
  * Better performance   
  * Components by default are server components.   
  * Can use async/await within the component, without use of state management methods.   
  * Can't use any kind of hook.   
  * Can't assign any event handlers.   
* ![Client Essentially the same kind of React components Component you are already used to using Bends the rules of traditional components a Server little bit Components Usually we want to use server components\! **Adding Dynamic Paths** 

* \[page\] will match any pattern in the URL path, for creating dynamic paths.   
  * The dynamic path will show up as a prop with a string value.   
  * The name of the prop will match what you put in the \[\] when created the dynamic path. 

**Async Dynamic Params** 

* Dynamic params are now asynchronous in Next 15\. We will need to await params before we can access.   
* [https://nextjs.org/docs/messages/sync-dynamic-apis](https://nextjs.org/docs/messages/sync-dynamic-apis) 

**Custom Not Found Pages** 

* not-found.tsx displays when we use notFound function.   
* Next.js will look for the closest not-found.tsx file whether in the current directory or in the parent(s) directory. 

**Automatic Loading Spinners** 

* loading.tsx is displayed when a server component is fetching some data. 

   
**Server Actions in Great Detail**   
**Server Actions in Nextjs Client Components** 

* You cannot define a server action in a client component.   
* One way to use a server action in a client component is to define the server action in a server component and pass it as props to the client component.   
  * ![Server Actions in Client SnippetEditPage Components Server Component Option \#1 export default function SnippetEditPage () { async function updateSnippet(id, code) { 'use server' ; Define the Server Action in // Code to update the snippet a Server Component and } pass it as props to the return ( \<SnippetEditForm onSubmit={updateSnippet} /\> Client Component ); Server components can't pass event handlers down to snippet client components - this is the one exception SnippetEditForm Client Component Monaco Editor][image7]  
  * Server components can't pass event handlers down to client components – this is the one exception   
* Second way is to create a separate file for server actions and import it in a client component.   
  * ![Server Actions in Client Define the Server Action in Components a separate file and import Option \#2 it into the Client Component actions.ts 'use server' ; SnippetEditForm export async function updateSnippet(id, code) { // code to update the snippet Client Component // code to redirect the user Making server actions in a separate file? You only have to write 'use server' once at the top of the file][image8]

**Options for Calling Server Actions from Client Components** 

* StartTransition makes sure we transition to another page after the data has been updated.   
* First option allows forms to work even if user isn't running Javascript in their browser.   
  * Pointless in this case since our form requires JS for monaco editior.   
  * ![Calling Server Actions from Client Components Option \#1 Client Component 'use client import \* as actions from 'actions' ; function ClientComponent () { const \[code, setCode\] = useState('') ; 'use server' // Make sure 'editSnippet' gets called with the code from editor export async function editSnippet(code: string, formData: FormData) { const editSnippetAction = // update snippet actions. editSnippet bind(null, code) ; return \<form action={editSnippetAction}\> We used 'bind' to customize the arguments][image9]  
* Second option doesn't need to mess with 'bind' function. It's closer to classic React behavior.   
  * ![Calling Server Actions from Client Components Option \#2 Client Component 'use client' import { startTransition } from 'react' ; import \* as actions from 'actions' ; function ClientComponent () { 'use server' const \[code, setCode\] = useState(' ') ; export async function editSnippet(code: string) { const handleClick = () =\> { // update snippet startTransition async () =\> { await actions.editSnippet(code) ; } ; Not tied to a 'form', so only the arguments passed directly to the return \<button onClick={handleClick}\> server action are received Submit \</button\> Makes sure we have updated data before we attempt to navigate][image10]  
* ![Client Component Client Component 'use client' import \* as actions from 'actions' ; 'use client import \* as actions from 'actions' ; function ClientComponent () { 'use server' const \[code, setCode\] = useState(' ') ; function ClientComponent () { export async function editSnippet ( const \[code, setCode\] = useState('') ; 'use server' // Make sure 'editSnippet' gets called code: string, with the code from editor formData: FormData const handleClick = async () =\> { export async function editSnippet( code: string const editSnippetAction = editSnippet await actions.editSnippet(code) ; .bind(null, code) ; // update snippet F: // update snippet return \<button onClick={handleClick}\> return \<form action={editSnippetAction}\> ][image11]

**UseActionState in Next v15** 

* useFormState was renamed to useActionState in React 19\.   
* [https://react.dev/reference/react/useActionState](https://react.dev/reference/react/useActionState) 

**UseForm State in action**   
**Breaking Changes in Forms with React 19** 

* In React 19, forms are now reset after submission by default.   
* [https://github.com/facebook/react/issues/29034\#issuecomment-2143595195](https://github.com/facebook/react/issues/29034#issuecomment-2143595195)   
* Use the startTransition hook to mitigate the resetting of the form. 

**Adding the Form Validation**   
**Gotchas Around Error Handling in Nextjs** 

* error.tsx is rendered when an error occurs in a server component   
  * Must be a client component. This is a hard requirement.   
* ErrorPageProps interface has two props:   
  * error, which is an Error type object   
  * reset, which is a function that allows us to refresh a route

**The Full Route Cache System** 

* ![Caching Next implements caching in several locations. Can lead to unexpected behavior Data Cache Responses from requests made with 'fetch' are stored and used across requests. Router Cache 'Soft' navigation between routes are cached in the browser and reused when a user revisits a page. Request Make two or more 'GET' requests with 'fetch' during a user's Memoization request to your server? Only one 'GET' is actually executed. Full Route At build time, Next decides if your route is static or dynamic. If Cache it is static, the page is rendered and the result is stored. In production, users are given this pre-rendered result.][image13]

* ![Time-Based Every X seconds, ignore the cached response and fetch new data Every 3 seconds the next request to this route will trigger a rerender export const revalidate = 3; export default async function Page () { const snippets = await db . snippets. findMany() ; return \<div\>{snippets.map( .. )}\</div\> }][image18]  
* ![On-Demand Forcibly purge a cached response Dump cache for everything in a page import { revalidatePath } from "next/cache"; / / When we think data that the '/snippets' // route uses has changed ... revalidatePath('/snippets' ) ;][image19]
